", x)) ``` ::: # Purpose - Train the two custom BirdNET classifiers from code, with a fixed random seed (123), so the fitting is reproducible - Choose the hyperparameters (among 30 configurations drawn at random) and the classification thresholds, and estimate the performance of the classifiers, by 5-fold cross-validation grouped by recording - Classify the vocalizations of other bellbirds and of the focal bellbird with models that never heard them The two classifiers are: - **Sympatric + allopatric**: the three sympatric species the bellbird could have imitated (Keel-billed Toucan, Collared Aracari and Montezuma Oropendola), their closely related allopatric species (Choco Toucan, Pale-mandibled Aracari and Chestnut-headed Oropendola) and the Three-wattled Bellbird - **Sympatric only**: the three sympatric species and the Three-wattled Bellbird # Data 2 s clips exported in [Data preparation](birdnet_acoustic_data_prep.qmd). All clips are used for cross-validation; each recording contributes several clips. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} folds <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "folds.csv")) clips <- aggregate(clip ~ species, folds, length) names(clips) <- c("Species", "Clips") clips$Recordings <- as.integer(tapply(folds$recording, folds$species, function(x) length(unique(x)))[clips$Species]) clips$Type <- ifelse(clips$Species %in% sympatric_spp, "Sympatric", "Allopatric") clips$Type[clips$Species == "Procnias tricarunculatus"] <- "Bellbird" clips[, c("Species", "Type", "Recordings", "Clips")] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|Species |Type | Recordings| Clips| |:--------------------------|:----------|----------:|-----:| |Procnias tricarunculatus |Bellbird | 59| 800| |Psarocolius guatimozinus |Allopatric | 15| 410| |Psarocolius montezuma |Sympatric | 42| 815| |Pteroglossus erythropygius |Allopatric | 45| 866| |Pteroglossus torquatus |Sympatric | 35| 462| |Ramphastos brevis |Allopatric | 36| 808| |Ramphastos sulfuratus |Sympatric | 27| 1356|
::: ::: # Cross-validation design - The clips were split into 5 folds with a stratified group k-fold (seed 123): all clips of a recording fall in the same fold, and the folds are balanced by species. Five folds keep about 3 recordings of the species with fewest recordings (*P. guatimozinus*, 15) in each fold - For each fold, the classifiers were trained on the other 4 folds and classified the held-out fold, so every clip has one out-of-fold prediction from a model that never heard its recording - Training stops early on a random 20% of the training clips (the held-out fold is not used for training in any way), up to 50 epochs; the weights of the best epoch are kept - Training and classification use a 400–12,000 Hz bandpass, BirdNET-Analyzer v2.4 and seed 123 - Hyperparameters were chosen by random search: 30 configurations (R01–R30) drawn at random (seed 123, [`scripts/birdnet_random_search.py`](https://github.com/maRce10/bellbird_vocal_mimicry/blob/master/scripts/birdnet_random_search.py)) over the search space of BirdNET-Analyzer's built-in tuner: hidden units (0–2,048), dropout (0–0.9), batch size (8–128) with its own set of learning rates (0.0001–0.1), upsampling ratio (0–1) and mode (repeat, mean, linear), mixup, label smoothing and focal loss (γ 0.5–4, α 0.1–0.9). Random search samples the whole search space instead of a few values of each hyperparameter (as a grid does), so with the same number of trainings it tries more distinct values of the hyperparameters that matter most - The selection rule was set before looking at the results of the random search, and uses only the reference species (never the focal bellbird), separately for each classifier: the score is the macro-averaged AUPRC of the out-of-fold predictions (threshold-free, every species weighted equally), and among the configurations within one standard error of the best one (SD across folds / √5) the simplest is chosen (one-standard-error rule): fewest hidden units, then fewest added techniques (focal loss, mixup, label smoothing, upsampling), then lowest dropout - The out-of-fold score of the best of 30 configurations is optimistic, because part of its advantage is chance. To estimate the performance of the whole procedure (search, selection and threshold tuning), for each fold the configuration was chosen and its thresholds tuned on the other 4 folds only, and it was then scored on that fold - Per-species thresholds are the ones that maximize F1 on the out-of-fold predictions (0.05 steps); a clip is assigned to the species with the highest confidence if it reaches that species' threshold, otherwise it is left unassigned The whole pipeline is run with [`scripts/birdnet_cv.sh`](https://github.com/maRce10/bellbird_vocal_mimicry/blob/master/scripts/birdnet_cv.sh). It assigns the folds with [`scripts/birdnet_cv_folds.py`](https://github.com/maRce10/bellbird_vocal_mimicry/blob/master/scripts/birdnet_cv_folds.py) and trains through [`scripts/train_birdnet.py`](https://github.com/maRce10/bellbird_vocal_mimicry/blob/master/scripts/train_birdnet.py), a wrapper of BirdNET-Analyzer that seeds Python, NumPy and TensorFlow (weights, shuffling, dropout, mixup), turns on deterministic TensorFlow operations and saves the training history. Re-running the training with the same seed gives the same models up to floating-point rounding. ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} # from the project root python scripts/birdnet_random_search.py data/processed/birdnet_cv/random_search_configs.csv --n 30 --seed 123 bash scripts/birdnet_cv.sh all # folds, 300 trainings (30 configurations x 2 classifiers x 5 folds) and classifications ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cv_res <- list() for (cf in configs) for (m in models) { sc <- oof_scores(cf, m, folds) spp <- model_spp[[m]] thr <- r$metrics$macro[["accuracy"]], check.names = FALSE) })))) cmp_cv$Model <- factor(cmp_cv$Model, levels = model_labels) # one-standard-error rule (see Cross-validation design) complexity <- auprc <- setNames(d$AUPRC, d$Configuration) top <- names(auprc)[which.max(auprc)] select_one_se(auprc, d$`AUPRC SD`[d$Configuration == top] / sqrt(5), complexity[[m]]) }) cmp_cv$Selected <- ifelse(cmp_cv$Configuration == best_cfg[match(cmp_cv$Model, model_labels)], "✓", "") cmp_cv$`Within 1 SE of best` <- "" for (m in models) { i <- which(cmp_cv$Model == model_labels[[m]]) top <- Validation: the random 20% of the training clips used for early stopping. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hist <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(k) { h <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "models", best_cfg[[m]], m, paste0("fold_", k), paste0(m, "_history.csv"))) data.frame(model = paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")"), fold = k, epoch = rep(h$epoch, 4), metric = rep(c("Loss", "Loss", "AUPRC", "AUPRC"), each = nrow(h)), set = rep(c("Training", "Validation", "Training", "Validation"), each = nrow(h)), value = c(h$loss, h$val_loss, h$AUPRC, h$val_AUPRC)) })))) hist$model <- factor(hist$model, levels = unique(hist$model)) ggplot(hist, aes(epoch, value, color = set, group = interaction(set, fold))) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) + facet_grid(metric ~ model, scales = "free") + scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.7, name = "") + labs(x = "Epoch", y = "") + theme(legend.position = "top", strip.background = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](birdnet_model_fitting_files/figure-html/training history-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: # Performance of the selected configurations ```{.r .cell-code} for (m in models) { r <- cv_res[[best_cfg[[m]]]][[m]] ps <- r$metrics$per_species names(ps) <- c("Species", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "AUPRC", "Threshold", "Clips") cat("\n\n##", model_labels[[m]], "(configuration", best_cfg[[m]], ")\n\n") print(kable(ps, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)) } ``` ## Confusion matrices ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cv_conf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) { r <- cv_res[[best_cfg[[m]]]][[m]] tb <- as.data.frame(table(true = r$scores$true, predicted = r$metrics$pred)) tb$prop <- tb$Freq / ave(tb$Freq, tb$true, FUN = sum) tb$model <- paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")") tb })) cv_conf$model <- factor(cv_conf$model, levels = unique(cv_conf$model)) cv_conf$true <- short(as.character(cv_conf$true)) cv_conf$predicted <- short(as.character(cv_conf$predicted)) conf_plot <- function(label, title) { ggplot(cv_conf, aes(predicted, true, fill = prop)) + geom_tile(color = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3.5, color = ifelse(cv_conf$prop > 0.5, "black", "white")) + facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free") + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Proportion\nof true class") + labs(x = "Predicted", y = "True", title = title) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic"), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.background = element_blank()) } conf_plot(ifelse(cv_conf$Freq > 0, cv_conf$Freq, ""), "Out-of-fold predictions (number of clips)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](birdnet_model_fitting_files/figure-html/cv confusion-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: Normalized confusion matrices (each row divided by the number of clips of the true class, so rows sum to 1 and the diagonal is the recall of each class; blank cells: no clips; <0.01: at least one clip but below 0.005): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} conf_plot(ifelse(cv_conf$Freq == 0, "", ifelse(cv_conf$prop < 0.005, "<0.01", sprintf("%.2f", cv_conf$prop))), "Out-of-fold predictions (proportion of the true class)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](birdnet_model_fitting_files/figure-html/cv confusion normalized-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: ## ::: ::: # Focal bellbird classification The 1660 focal bellbird clips are classified with the 5 fold models of the selected configuration: the confidence of each species is averaged across the 5 models (ensemble) and the out-of-fold thresholds are applied. The predictions are saved in `data/processed/birdnet_cv/focal_predictions_.csv`, and the out-of-fold predictions of the reference clips in `data/processed/birdnet_cv/oof_predictions_.csv`; both are used in the [statistical analysis](statistical_analysis_cv.qmd). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} focal_cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) { cf <- best_cfg[[m]] en <- ensemble_scores(cf, m) en$predicted <- assign_species(en, model_spp[[m]], cv_res[[cf]][[m]]$thr) write.csv(en, file.path(cv_dir, paste0("focal_predictions_", m, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE) data.frame(model = model_labels[[m]], predicted = en$predicted) })) # out-of-fold predictions of the reference clips, for downstream use for (m in models) { r <- cv_res[[best_cfg[[m]]]][[m]] write.csv(data.frame(r$scores, predicted = r$metrics$pred, check.names = FALSE), file.path(cv_dir, paste0("oof_predictions_", m, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE) } # predictions of every configuration (out-of-fold, and focal ensemble), for the robustness # check of the statistical analysis all_pred <- do.call(rbind, lapply(configs, function(cf) do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) { r <- cv_res[[cf]][[m]] en <- ensemble_scores(cf, m) rbind(data.frame(config = cf, model = m, clip = r$scores$clip, true = r$scores$true, predicted = r$metrics$pred), data.frame(config = cf, model = m, clip = en$clip, true = "focal", predicted = assign_species(en, model_spp[[m]], r$thr))) })))) write.csv(all_pred, file.path(cv_dir, "predictions_all_configurations.csv"), row.names = FALSE) write.csv(data.frame(model = names(best_cfg), config = best_cfg), file.path(cv_dir, "selected_configurations.csv"), row.names = FALSE) fc_tab <- as.data.frame(table(focal_cv$model, focal_cv$predicted)) names(fc_tab) <- c("Model", "Classified as", "Clips") fc_tab[fc_tab$Clips > 0, ] ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ::: # Takeaways - Both classifiers were trained from code with a fixed seed (123); re-running gives the same models up to floating-point rounding - Among 30 configurations drawn at random, 5-fold cross-validation grouped by recording selected configuration R19 for the sympatric + allopatric classifier (out-of-fold macro AUPRC 0.884) and R23 for the sympatric-only classifier (0.993); the procedure, scored on folds not used to choose the configuration, gave macro AUPRC 0.888 and 0.993 - The weakest classes are the aracaris and the oropendolas in the sympatric + allopatric classifier, where each is confused with its close relative (*P. torquatus* with *P. erythropygius* above all); in the sympatric-only classifier all species have F1 > 0.95 - Other bellbirds were rarely classified as another species (out-of-fold predictions of all their recordings) - 807 focal bellbird clips were classified as a sympatric species and 80 as an allopatric one (10.1 : 1) --- Session information ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu Running under: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS Matrix products: default BLAS: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/blas/libblas.so.3.10.0 LAPACK: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/lapack/liblapack.so.3.10.0 LAPACK version 3.10.0 locale: [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C [3] LC_TIME=es_CR.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8 [5] LC_MONETARY=es_CR.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 [7] LC_PAPER=es_CR.UTF-8 LC_NAME=C [9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=es_CR.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C time zone: America/Costa_Rica tzcode source: system (glibc) attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base other attached packages: [1] knitr_1.52 viridis_0.6.5 viridisLite_0.4.3 ggplot2_4.0.3 loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] vctrs_0.7.3 cli_3.6.6 rlang_1.3.0 xfun_0.61 [5] otel_0.2.0 generics_0.1.4 S7_0.2.2 jsonlite_2.0.0 [9] labeling_0.4.3 glue_1.8.1 htmltools_0.5.9 gridExtra_2.3.1 [13] scales_1.4.0 rmarkdown_2.32 grid_4.6.1 tibble_3.3.1 [17] evaluate_1.0.5 fastmap_1.2.0 yaml_2.3.12 lifecycle_1.0.5 [21] compiler_4.6.1 dplyr_1.2.1 RColorBrewer_1.1-3 pkgconfig_2.0.3 [25] htmlwidgets_1.6.4 farver_2.1.2 digest_0.6.39 R6_2.6.1 [29] tidyselect_1.2.1 pillar_1.11.1 magrittr_2.0.5 withr_3.0.3 [33] tools_4.6.1 gtable_0.3.6 ``` ::: :::
